record.paper_title: Causal Machine Learning: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Causal machine learning lacks a mature open-source ecosystem comparable to common machine-learning frameworks. How can libraries and APIs be built for identification tests, structural causal model manipulation and inference, causal benchmarks, and pre-trained structural causal models so researchers can prototype and compare methods more easily?

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, there is a much smaller open source ecosystem for learning or performing inference with SCMs.

At the time of this writing, we are unaware of software libraries providing APIs for convenient identification tests, manipulating SCMs, or importing causal benchmarks (Chapter 9) as well as pre-trained SCMs to facilitate progress on novel research ideas.
Providing convenient APIs for such algorithms would be immensely helpful.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Design and construct an open-source software ecosystem for causal machine learning analogous to standard machine-learning frameworks. Concretely, specify the architecture, abstractions, and application programming interfaces (APIs) of libraries that provide:

1. Identification tests: routines that, given a structural causal model (SCM) or a causal graph G = (V, E) together with an interventional or counterfactual query (e.g., P(Y | do(X = x))), determine whether the query is identifiable from observational and/or experimental distributions, and if so return an estimand in terms of observed quantities (e.g., via the ID algorithm or do-calculus).

2. Manipulation and inference with SCMs: data structures for representing an SCM M = (U, V, F, P(U)) — exogenous variables U with distribution P(U), endogenous variables V, and structural assignments F = {f_v : v ∈ V} — together with operations for interventions (do-operators), counterfactual evaluation, abduction–action–prediction, marginalization, mutilation of graphs, and sampling.

3. Causal benchmarks: a standardized interface for importing curated datasets (with ground-truth causal graphs, interventional distributions, or counterfactual labels) for evaluating causal discovery, causal effect estimation, and counterfactual inference algorithms.

4. Pre-trained SCMs: a model hub providing serialized, ready-to-use structural causal models that researchers can load, fine-tune, intervene on, and compare against.

State a precise specification (data types, function signatures, semantic guarantees) for such an ecosystem, and exhibit a reference implementation enabling researchers to prototype new identification, discovery, and estimation methods and to compare them on shared benchmarks under a uniform API.
artifact.status_search_result: Causal ML libraries (DoWhy, EconML, CausalNex, Ananke, pgmpy, causal-learn, pyAgrum) provide partial functionality such as identification (DoWhy implements the ID algorithm) and effect estimation, but a unified ecosystem covering identification tests, SCM manipulation, standardized causal benchmarks, and a hub of pre-trained SCMs does not yet exist. The problem is therefore best characterized as still open / actively being addressed in pieces.

status_evidence.title: DoWhy: An End-to-End Library for Causal Inference
status_evidence.snippet: DoWhy supports identification of causal effects using do-calculus and the ID algorithm, but does not provide a model hub of pre-trained SCMs or unified benchmark imports.
status_evidence.claim: Partial libraries exist but no unified ecosystem matching all four requested components.

status_evidence.title: causal-learn: a Python package for causal discovery
status_evidence.snippet: causal-learn offers causal discovery algorithms but not identification testing APIs or pre-trained SCM repositories.
status_evidence.claim: Coverage of components is fragmented across separate libraries.

status_evidence.title: Ananke: Python package for causal inference with graphical models
status_evidence.snippet: Ananke implements identification in graphical models including hidden variable settings, but lacks integration with benchmarks and pre-trained SCMs.
status_evidence.claim: No single ecosystem currently integrates identification, SCM manipulation, benchmarks, and pre-trained models.
